utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, everybody. I will ask the registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-95-17-I, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Bralo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the appearances, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, Counsel. My name is Mark Harmon. Appearing with me today is Fergal Gaynor to my right, and to my left is Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Virginia Lindsay on behalf of Miroslav Bralo and I'm being assisted by an interpreter, Snezana Bukal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please sit down, Madam. I believe you have the assistance of an interpreter. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who I believe is not part of the Defence team as such, is that right, so far? But she will be part of the Defence team soon. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bralo, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. A short reminder of the proceedings so far. Pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, an initial appearance in this case was held on the 15th of November, 2004. And during the hearing, I explained to the parties what the case was about and I asked Mr. Bralo whether he was ready and willing to plead during the hearing. As is set forth by the Rules, he can also wait for 30 days, within which time period he can make up his mind. And Mr. Bralo decided to think it over to examine the indictment in order to plead knowing the circumstances, and that he would do so later on. So within the time limits set by the Rules, which is 30 days, so pursuant to the rules, we are holding today this further appearance hearing in order to finalise the work which was started on the 15th of November, 2004. Pursuant to the Rules of this Tribunal, the indictment, as decided by the indictee, can be either read out in it entirety or, alternatively, it is possible to read only the counts charged against the accused so that he can plead guilty or not guilty to each of the counts. So I'm going to put the question again today. Mr. Bralo, do you want the indictment to be read out in its entirety or do you waive this right and are you happy for the counts only to be read so that you can plead guilty or not guilty? This is the question I'm putting to you, Mr. Bralo. Do you wish the indictment to be read out?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no need to read the entire indictment. I am familiar with the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. My second question is as follows: As much as you say you are familiar with the indictment, you realise that among the counts in the indictment there is the chapeau as it is called, which is the general explanation for each of the counts, the general allegations. Let me give you an example and you can discuss this with your counsel if you so wish. For instance, paragraph 15 of the indictment, it has to do with general allegations leading to Counts 1 and 2. Do you also waive the right of having the -- those headings or introductions read out? And are you -- do you just wish the counts as such to be read out. Is that right? You said yes, you answered yes to this question, too. Is that right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before going any further, however, I wish to remind you of the background of this case. As I did during the hearing held on 15th of November, I sort of gave you in broad terms the charges against Mr. Bralo. The period involved goes from April 1993 to June 1993, and there are allegations against Mr. Bralo, who's charged with committing acts that are tantamount to crimes falling under Articles 2 and 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal, namely grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions, as under Article 2 of the Statute, as well as crimes -- war crimes which are also under Article 3 of the same Statute. To bring the previous hearing, there was a small detail of disagreement between what was stated in the indictment and what Mr. Bralo said concerning his position or his work before the armed conflict. As stated in the indictment, Mr. Bralo was said to have been working in a company called Slobodan Princip Seljo, whilst Mr. Bralo said he never worked in the said company. At the time, I put the question to the Prosecution to ask whether the detail was relevant or not in the indictment. Mr. Harmon, do you think that this is a relevant detail that will have consequences on the identity of the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand very well because you were not present at the hearing. There was a minor detail, the fact that the -- an Accused B is mentioned in the indictment, whereas the current indictment only mentions one accused. So anyone who doesn't know the whole history of the case would not be able to understand who is the Accused B, since we only have one accused here. So during the last hearing, I'd asked for some clarification on this point and how the Prosecutor was planning to go about providing a clearer indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am prepared to make certain amendments to this indictment to clarify that issue. I believe Accused B was someone who had been previously accused --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... from my indictment that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I follow you perfectly. However, the problems remain -- the problem remains. Anyone reading this indictment today will wonder who this Accused B is because he's nowhere to be found, this Accused B. Isn't it right? I mean, initially there were four of them, that's the whole background of the case; I'm not going to go into details right now. But I think it is worth looking into the matter. The Prosecution had better look into this so that Mr. Bralo be fully aware of what he's pleading today when he does so. So if you wish us to go into private session in order to provide some explanation on this point, so that Mr. Bralo can really plead being fully aware of all the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Registrar, can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in open session. Mr. Registrar, I shall ask you to read out only the counts in -- there are 21 of them, 21 counts against Mr. Bralo. Mr. Registrar, once you have finished reading each of the counts, please stop so that I can ask Mr. Bralo whether he pleads guilty or not guilty. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Count 1: Grave breach (unlawful confinement of civilians), as recognised by Article 2 (G) of the Tribunal's Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead? Please stand up, Mr. Bralo. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Second count, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI

utterances.text: Count 21, violation of the laws or customs of war (outrages upon personal dignity including rape), recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal's Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. How do you plead, Mr. Bralo, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. [In English] Thank you. [Interpretation] I have just been told that there was no interpretation regarding Counts 9 and 13 as well as Count 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: I believe also Count 7 is reflected as a guilty plea. It should be not guilty. And also Count 11 does not have an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I believe that I myself put the question again of Mr. Bralo, because I heard "guilty," but he confirmed that he had pleaded not guilty, didn't he? So you mentioned Count 7 as well. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're going to check together. I hope you don't mind. So Count 7, Count 9, Count 13, and Count 16. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: And -- well, if -- and I thought also Count 11, but if that was correctly recorded --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, better be safe than sorry. Thank you. So I will ask Mr. Registrar to read those counts again, starting with Count 7.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 7: Grave breach (torture or inhumane treatment), recognised by Article 2(b) of the Tribunal's Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. Bralo, there was a problem with the interpretation. So I'm going to ask you to answer this count again. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Let's move on to Count 9.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Please sit down. So I am now able to confirm that Mr. Bralo pleaded not guilty to each count. I wanted to avoid any incident arising from the translation or interpretation. So with regard to each and every count in the indictment, it is now clear that Mr. Bralo has pleaded not guilty. So at this juncture I will turn to Mr. Harmon. Do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do not, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm now turning to the Defence. Do you have anything to add, Ms. Lindsay?

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One question I'd like to put to you is as follows: Did you inquire about the health and detention condition of Mr. Bralo? As far as you know, does he have any health problems? Do you want to warn me or let me know of anything in open or in private session as is necessary? We can move into private session if you want to.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: That's not necessary, Your Honour. I did inquire and there are no representations to be made at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You can sit down. So pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence which says under VI -- V: "In case of a plea of not guilty, instruct the registrar to set a date for the trial." So pursuant to the provision under Roman V in Rule 62, I shall instruct the registrar to set a date for trial. This being said, I believe that I can now declare the hearing adjourned, and I thank everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.17 p.m.
